guarantees.claim: When key_length_i is Key_128, Key_256, Key_384, or Key_512, the combinational pad outputs are built by taking the corresponding most significant bits of secret_key_i (1023:896, 1023:768, 1023:640, 1023:512), zero-extending to the block size (BlockSizeSHA256 or BlockSizeSHA512), and bitwise XORing with the appropriate pad constant (0x36 for i_pad, 0x5c for o_pad).

When key_length_i is Key_1024, i_pad_256 and o_pad_256 are explicitly set to all zeros; i_pad_512 = secret_key_i[1023:0] XORed with {(BlockSizeSHA512/8){8'h36}} and o_pad_512 = secret_key_i[1023:0] XORed with {(BlockSizeSHA512/8){8'h5c}}.
When key_length_i does not match any of the explicit case items (default), all four pad signals retain their initial all-zeros value because the default case is empty.
guarantees.cond: key_length_i not in {Key_128, Key_256, Key_384, Key_512, Key_1024}

assumptions.claim: key_length_i must always be one of the defined legal values (Key_128, Key_256, Key_384, Key_512, Key_1024) to produce valid HMAC key pads; the block provides no fallback error signaling.
assumptions.risk: If an illegal key_length_i appears, all pads become zero, potentially causing silent HMAC computation with a zeroed inner/outer pad, leading to incorrect authentication tags.

assumptions.claim: The parameters BlockSizeSHA256 and BlockSizeSHA512 must equal 512 and 1024 respectively (the standard SHA-2 block sizes in bits).
assumptions.risk: Incorrect parameter values cause wrong zero-padding lengths, leading to HMAC key pad misalignment and interoperability failure.

assumptions.claim: secret_key_i must present the actual key material left-aligned within its 1024-bit bus, i.e., the most significant bits contain the key; for keys shorter than 1024 bits the lower bits are ignored (or padded with zeros externally).
assumptions.risk: If the key is right-aligned or arbitrarily packed, the extracted secret_key_i bits will not match the intended key, leading to an incorrect HMAC result.

uncertain_points.claim: The default case produces all-zero pads with no error output. If an illegal key_length_i can reach this block (e.g., via a register bit flip), the HMAC engine may continue operating with effectively a zeroed key without any alert.
uncertain_points.risk: Silent HMAC degradation and potential undetected authentication failures.

uncertain_points.claim: The code comment says Key_1024 'not allowed to be configured for SHA-2 256' and zeroes the 256-bit pads, but it is unclear whether upper-level configuration logic prevents HMAC_SHA256 mode when a 1024-bit key is selected. If the prevention is missing, the SHA-256 datapath could use a zeroed pad, seriously compromising security.
uncertain_points.cond: Key_1024 is selected and SHA-256 operation is enabled
uncertain_points.risk: HMAC with zeroed inner/outer pad essentially uses a known key, breaking authentication.

uncertain_points.claim: The left-alignment assumption for secret_key_i and the exact bit ranges used for each key length are not documented within the code block; external documentation or CSR specifications should confirm this mapping.
uncertain_points.risk: Misunderstanding by integrators could lead to key misplacement and HMAC failure.
